label: Predicative Adverbs
description: A 20-question check on predicative/impersonal state adverbs.

questions.prompt: What does «Мне надо идти домой» mean in English?
questions.explain: «Надо» is the impersonal predicative of necessity, the dative «мне» names who must act, and the infinitive «идти» gives the action: 'I need to go home.'

questions.prompt: In «Тебе надо больше отдыхать», what case is «тебе» and what is its role?
options: Dative experiencer who needs to act
questions.explain: Impersonal constructions with «надо» take a dative experiencer, so «тебе» marks the person who needs to rest.

questions.prompt: How would you say 'May I come in?' in Russian, as in the lesson?
questions.explain: «Можно мне войти?» uses «можно» for permission with the dative «мне» and the infinitive «войти», the standard polite request at a doorway.

questions.prompt: What does «Здесь можно курить?» ask?
options: Is it hard to smoke here?
questions.explain: «Можно» is the impersonal predicative for what is permitted, so the question asks whether smoking is allowed here.

questions.prompt: Which word in «Раньше здесь можно было плавать» marks the past tense?
questions.explain: The neuter «было» puts the impersonal «можно» into the past: swimming was once allowed here.

questions.prompt: What does «Здесь невозможно работать» mean?
options: It is necessary to work here.
It is impossible to work here.
questions.explain: «Невозможно» is the impersonal predicative meaning 'it is impossible', so working here cannot be done.

questions.prompt: Complete the request for more tea: «Можно мне ещё ___?»
questions.explain: The lesson phrase «Можно мне ещё чаю?» uses the partitive genitive «чаю» to ask for a portion of tea.

questions.prompt: What does «Мне трудно дышать здесь» mean?
options: It is easy for me to breathe here.
It is hard for me to breathe here.
questions.explain: «Трудно» means 'hard/difficult' with the dative experiencer «мне», so it is hard for me to breathe here.

questions.prompt: In «Сначала всегда трудно», why is there no infinitive?
options: «Трудно» can stand alone as a complete impersonal predicate
Infinitives are never used with трудно
questions.explain: «Трудно» works as a complete impersonal predicate on its own, stating the general truth that the start is always hard.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'I need to rest a little' (slightly formal), as in the lesson?
questions.explain: «Мне нужно отдохнуть немного» uses «нужно» (need) with the dative «мне» and the infinitive «отдохнуть».

questions.prompt: In «Ей надо позвонить врачу», why are there two dative-like forms?
options: «Ей» is the experiencer; «врачу» is the dative object of «позвонить»
questions.explain: «Ей» is the dative experiencer who must act, while «врачу» is a second dative governed by the verb «позвонить» (to call).

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses 'It was impossible to fall asleep'?
questions.explain: «Было невозможно уснуть» uses neuter «было» to make «невозможно» past, with the infinitive «уснуть».

questions.prompt: What does «Всё понятно, спасибо» convey?
options: It is all clear, thank you.
questions.explain: «Понятно» is the impersonal predicative meaning 'clear/understood', so the phrase says it is all clear and thanks.

questions.prompt: In «Объясни ещё раз, непонятно», what does «непонятно» mean?
questions.explain: The negated form «непонятно», written as one word, states that something is not clear, prompting another explanation.

questions.prompt: What does «Отсюда хорошо видно море» mean?
options: The sea is far from here.
It is hard to see the sea from here.
The sea can be clearly seen from here.
We must look at the sea.
questions.explain: «Видно» is the impersonal predicative of visibility, with accusative «море» as what can be seen from this vantage point.

questions.prompt: In «В тумане ничего не видно», what is being said?
options: Nothing can be seen in the fog.
Everything is visible in the fog.
We must wait for the fog.
questions.explain: The impersonal «видно» with «не» and «ничего» states that nothing can be seen, with «в тумане» giving the cause.

questions.prompt: What does «Ладно, я согласен» express?
questions.explain: «Ладно» is a colloquial discourse word meaning 'fine/okay', here signalling that the speaker accepts the proposal.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly grants permission to one person to rest today?
questions.explain: «Можно» grants permission, so «Тебе можно отдохнуть сегодня» means 'You may rest today'; «надо» would mean 'must' instead.

questions.prompt: What does «Наверное, завтра будет дождь» mean?
questions.explain: «Наверное» is a modal word meaning 'probably', hedging the prediction that it will rain tomorrow.

questions.prompt: In «Видимо, придётся ждать», what does the sentence express?
options: Apparently we will have to wait.
questions.explain: «Видимо» frames an inference ('apparently'), and impersonal «придётся» plus infinitive «ждать» states that waiting will be unavoidable.
